description:
pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:169-172 — the delta_base_num extraction:
  `// has_delta_crl_indicator confirmed OID presence above; None is unreachable.`
  `let delta_base_num = base_crl_number(&delta_crl)`
  `    .ok_or(Error::DeltaCrlBaseMismatch)?` // can only happen if code invariant broken`
  `    .map_err(Error::CrlParseError)?;`

base_crl_number looks up OID_DELTA_CRL_INDICATOR (2.5.29.27) — the same OID that has_delta_crl_indicator checks. After confirming has_delta_crl_indicator is true, base_crl_number is expected to return Some. The comment 'can only happen if code invariant broken' is correct.

BUT: base_crl_number returns None when the extension is absent. If has_delta_crl_indicator returns true (the OID is present) but base_crl_number returns None... that can only happen if there's a bug in has_delta_crl_indicator itself (impossible given both look up the same OID) or if the extensions slice is modified between calls (impossible in safe Rust).

So the .ok_or(Error::DeltaCrlBaseMismatch)? is dead code, but it's a reasonable defensive guard. Not a bug.

Actually noting a different issue: the check order in with_delta (lines 153-168) checks:
1. base CRL must NOT have deltaCRLIndicator
2. delta CRL MUST have deltaCRLIndicator

But then at line 174-179 it checks issuer match. The issuer check happens AFTER the CRL numbers are extracted. If the issuers don't match, we've already done work. Minor efficiency concern only. No bug.

Not filing a separate issue.
title: CRL DeltaCRL indicator: base_crl_number called without has_delta_crl_indicator guard
